paragraphs: The Bord Gáis Energy Theatre is a big theatre in Dublin. It made a profit of €5 million in 2025.
Almost 600,000 people went to shows there last year. They saw shows like The Book of Mormon, Fiddler on the Roof and Moulin Rouge.
The theatre made a little less money than in 2024. In 2024, the famous musical Hamilton sold a lot of tickets.
The theatre has 56 workers. A family company owns it. The company bought the theatre in 2014.
The owners think 2026 will be a good year. Shows like Matilda and Mrs Doubtfire are coming. In 2027, there will be a new musical about Live Aid.
The Bord Gáis Energy Theatre in Dublin's docklands made a profit of €5 million last year, new company accounts show.

The theatre's income in 2025 was just under €17.7 million, a little lower than in 2024. That year, the hit musical Hamilton helped the theatre sell a record number of tickets. Tickets brought in €13.4 million in 2025, and food and drinks brought in €4.3 million. Almost 600,000 people went to see shows, including The Book of Mormon, Fiddler on the Roof and Moulin Rouge.

The theatre has an average of 56 staff. It is owned by Crownway Entertainment, a family company owned by John and Bernie Gallagher. They bought it in 2014 for €29.1 million. In 2024, they agreed a new 10-year deal with Bord Gáis Energy to keep its name on the building, worth around €2 million a year.

The company expects 2026 to be a strong year, with shows such as Matilda, To Kill a Mockingbird and Mrs Doubtfire. Next year, a new musical about the Live Aid concert, Just for One Day, will come to the theatre, along with Billy Elliot and Grease.
